system_context.module_and_spec_responsibility: The frozen design sections 2-5 assign preparation, identity and publication to the boot installer, read-only capability observation to the probe, package resolution to uv/upstream metadata, and extraction/JS invocation to yt-dlp. Section 6 assigns real-package execution evidence to CI-only scripts. .trellis/spec/wrapper/backend/dependency-sources.md:20 preserves boot-before-admission, :23 delegates Python/package policy to uv, :29 preserves explicit pins, :34 preserves binary integrity, and :40 requires validated offline reuse and prepare-before-retire. .trellis/spec/wrapper/backend/process-lifecycle.md:3 and :10 retain request ownership and shutdown cleanup. The candidate respects these directions without changing worker, pool, supervisor, request contracts or deployment pins.

spec_conformance_summary: Round-1 full source review against c2ce8adcbbe88ccd2b1ca1d4ad0113ee64954c84 found no blocking violation. Design SHA256 matches 76426AA7A6026E8C7EC860AC40EDD06B14B53149D8C727F9C1F283C98380426C; approval is present, frozen inputs/specs have no diff, and no task blocked.md or spec-gap.md is present. The shared default-extra requirement, additional identity field without schema change, old-ID rejection, shared EJS probe, prepare-before-publication and subsequent no-uv reuse conform to design sections 3-5 and PRD R1-R5. The real-image helper is reachable from hosted Docker CI and implements the approved offline bundle-load gate without moving logic into YAML or production. All ten implementation change responses were checked against source, including both new untracked Python files; there are no previous code-review findings to resolve. Expected coordinator bookkeeping changes were explicitly acknowledged and excluded from candidate criteria. PASS establishes source conformance only: reported lightweight mock checks are not native or real-image runtime proof. Hosted Linux/Windows tests, Docker execution, publication and registry/source-revision verification remain mandatory owner gates under section 7 and PRD R6/AC6. Live cookie-dependent YouTube extraction, PO Token, SABR and format availability remain unproven.
test_assertion_review: No unrelated assertion was removed or relaxed. (1) src/runtime_installer.rs:2553 changes the exact uv requirement assertion from bare yt-dlp to yt-dlp[default]; adjacent assertions retain stable-base selection, isolation, offline flags, no-build, copy mode, no-deps/system rejection and pip check. (2) tests/fixtures/managed_runtime.rs:25 adds EJS only through the fixture default-extra metadata; :36 supplies a separate deterministic EJS wheel. Both fixture callers now provide that wheelhouse. The shared wheel writer preserves RECORD generation; fixture solver bytes are not represented as upstream evidence. (3) src/runtime_installer.rs:1987 covers legacy identity with and without EJS. Assertions require the baseline-formula ID to differ, unavailable-uv preparation to fail without changing the old tree, no owned staging residue, same-pin replacement to restore the expected paths/identity, old-only removal, EJS inventory, fixed-root layout, and subsequent reuse with sources renamed away and uv missing without any root snapshot change. The EJS-present branch prevents missing-module failure from masking identity migration. (4) tests/runtime_install.rs:338 renames the dependency test to reflect default extras; its exact inventory count changes from two to three and adds the EJS version assertion. Explicit yt-dlp identity, mandatory dependency/version, successful resolution despite an absent unrelated optional-extra wheel, and missing-uv reuse remain. (5) tests/runtime_install.rs:399 requires missing default-wheel failure to identify EJS, publish no runtime and leave no staging; restoring the wheel must produce a single installation. (6) tests/runtime_install.rs:420 separately damages package, metadata, solver, each missing bundle and each empty bundle. Each case must reject reuse, preserve the damaged prior tree when uv is unavailable, clean owned staging and repair to the original identity. The unchanged assert_installed_plan at tests/runtime_install.rs:183 additionally checks path containment, schema/platform/pin, stable base, worker bytes/hash, artifact identities/hashes, installed binary hash, old-only removal and single installation. (7) scripts/tests/test_runtime_boot_smoke.py:59 adds helper non-invocation on invalid storage and exactly one resident invocation on success while retaining manifest-read assertions. :69 verifies exact installed isolated-Python stdin invocation. :78 verifies gate failure propagation, CLI shutdown before resident start, no network, missing uv, execution in the resident container, and stop/remove/volume cleanup. Existing real-entrypoint, stable-base, killed-shutdown, early-exit and no-pin-substitution assertions remain. (8) scripts/tests/test_runtime_ejs_smoke.py:36 checks Deno command restrictions, no granted permissions, checked exit, timeout, metadata lookup and lib/assignment/core/function-check/marker ordering. :61 and :70 require bare or metadata-less environments to fail before Deno. :76 checks missing/non-string/empty resources for both bundles. :93 rejects missing Deno, nonzero exit even with a marker, and timeout; :106 rejects zero exit without an exact marker line. These are mock-level negative/orchestration assertions, not actual Deno execution. (9) The real gate retains byte-identical manifest/log reuse, clean first shutdown and owned cleanup, and adds successful loading of both installed resources plus typeof jsc function evidence under offline Deno. No test claims a solved challenge. The reviewer ran no tests, builds or provisioning; native and real Docker assertions still require hosted execution.
